definition: Any imperfect development of the body, or any anomaly of organization.
Paralysis of the motor nerves; loss of movement.
Inability to utter articulate sounds, due either to paralysis of the larynx or to that form of aphasia, called motor, or ataxis, aphasia, due to loss of control of the muscles of speech.

(a) As used by some, inability to read aloud, due to brain disease. (b) More commonly, inability, due to brain disease, to understand written or printed symbols although they can be seen, as in case of word blindness.
Forgetfulness; also, a defect of speech, from cerebral disease, in which the patient substitutes wrong words or names in the place of those he wishes to employ. Quian.
Loss of the power of speech, or of the appropriate use of words, the vocal organs remaining intact, and the intelligence being preserved. It is dependent on injury or disease of the brain.
Incomplete or faulty development.
Partial privation or suspension of breath; suffocation.
The absence of bacteria, viruses, and other microorganisms.
Irregularity in disease, or in the functions.
A wasting away from want of nourishment; diminution in bulk or slow emaciation of the body or of any part.
Relating to atrophy.
Lack or loss of sight. Blindness.
Examination of the abdomen to detect abdominal disease.
Having a protuberant belly; pot-bellied.
Of or pertaining to the abdomen
an abnormal red blood cell having spiny projections.
An instrument for measuring the acuteness of the sense of hearing.
The measuring of the power or extent of hearing.
Chronic enlargement of the extremities and face.
That part of anatomy which describes the glands.
The part of physiology that treats of the glands.
Disease of a gland.
The hardening of a gland.
Dissection of, or incision into, a gland or glands.
Pain in a gland.
Glandular inflammation.
Glandlike; glandular.
A benign tumor of a glandlike structure; morbid enlargement of a gland.
Glandlike; glandular.
The digestion of fats.
Hydrolyzing fats; converting neutral fats into glycerin and free fatty acids, especially by the action of an enzyme.
Fatty; adipose.
Pertaining to, or derived from, fatty or oily substances; -- applied to certain acids obtained from fats by the action of nitric acid.
A mass of fat found internally; also, a fatty tumor.
Of or pertaining to animal fat
The state or condition of being an albino.
Pertaining to, or affected with albinism.
The state or condition of being an albino: abinoism; leucopathy.
That system of medical practice which aims to combat disease by the use of remedies which produce effects different from those produced by the special disease treated.
Changed or modified in nutritive power by the process of digestion.
Of or pertaining to allotropism.
of, relating to, resembling, or having aliveoli
A cell in a honeycomb.
Weakness of sight, without and opacity of the cornea, or of the interior of the eye.
Walking; moving from place to place.
To walk; to move about.
Of or pertaining to the membrane around the fetus.
Sexual generation.
That part of the starch granule or granulose which is soluble in water.
The formation of starch.
Forming starch
The conversion of starch into soluble products, as dextrins and sugar, especially by the action of enzymes.
Effecting the conversion of starch into soluble dextrin and sugar; as, an amylolytic ferment.
Instrument for determining the amount of starch in a substance.
A compound of the radical amyl with oxygen and a positive atom or radical.
Pertaining to, or derived from carbohydrates
Absence of sensibility to pain.
Lack of energy; inactivity.
a condition of absence of sensation
Want or defect of sight; blindness.
Want of appetite, without a loathing of food.
A morbid condition in which the blood is deficient in quality or in quantity.
Entire or partial loss or absence of feeling or sensation; a state of general or local insensibility produced by disease.
(a) Recovery of strength after sickness. (b) A species of epileptic attack, originating from gastric disorder.
The art of operation of restoring lost parts or the normal shape by the use of healthy tissue.

1. The art of dissecting, or artificially separating the different parts of any organized body, to discover their situation, structure, and economy; dissection. 2. The science which treats of the structure of organic bodies; anatomical structure or organization.
Dissection of the human body.
A terminal combining form: Having a stamen or stamens; staminate; as, monandrous, with one stamen; polyandrous, with many stamens.
A description of blood vessels and lymphatics.
That part of anatomy which treats of blood vessels and lymphatics.
Disease of the vessels, esp. the blood vessels.
An instrument for examining the capillary vessels of animals and plants. Morin.
Dissection of the blood vessels and lymphatics of the body. Dunglison.
A tumor composed chiefly of dilated blood vessels.

Stiffness or fixation of a joint; formation of a stiff joint. The union of two or more separate bones to from a single bone; the close union of bones or other structures in various animals. Same as Anchylosis.

Before, or toward the front, in place; as, the anterior part of the mouth; -- opposed to posterior. Note: In comparative anatomy, anterior often signifies at or toward the head, cephalic; and in human anatomy it is often used for ventral.
Prevention of sepsis by excluding or destroying microorganisms.
Of or pertaining to the aorta.
Inflammation of the aorta.
A marked prominence or process on any part of a bone.
Excision of the vermiform appendix.
Of or like an appendix.
Excision of the vermiform appendix.
Inflammation of the vermiform appendix.
Inflammation of an artery or arteries. Dunglison.

1. The trachea or windpipe. One of the vessels or tubes which carry either venous or arterial blood from the heart. They have tricker and more muscular walls than veins, and are connected with them by capillaries.
A systematic description of the arteries.
That part of anatomy which treats of arteries.
Abnormal thickening and hardening of the walls of the arteries, esp. of the intima, occurring mostly in old age.
The opening of an artery, esp. for bloodletting. Part of anatomy which treats of the dissection of the arteries.
Of or pertaining to the windpipe.
1. Of or pertaining to an artery, or the arteries; as, arterial action; the arterial system.
A small artery.
Surgical fixation of joints.
An affection characterized by pain in or about a joint, not dependent upon structural disease.
The description of joints.
That part of anatomy which treats of joints.
Any disease of the joints.
Articulation.
A strong scalpel used in the dissection of joints.
Any inflammation of the joints, particularly the gout.
To pronounce with a breathing.
An instrument for the evacuation of the fluid contents of tumors or collections of blood.
Of or pertaining to breathing; suited to the inhaling of air
(a) An encysted tumor containing curdy matter. (b) A disease characterized by thickening and fatty degeneration of the inner coat of the arteries.
Of or pertaining to an atrium.
The main part of either auricle of the heart as distinct from the auricular appendix. Also, the whole articular portion of the heart.
An instrument by which the power of hearing can be gauged and recorded on a scale.
Of or pertaining to hearing; auditory.
Of or pertaining to hearing, or to the sense or organs of hearing; as, the auditory nerve. The tube from the auditory meatus or opening of the ear to the tympanic membrane.
Having the form of the human ear; ear-shaped.
An instrument for examining the condition of the ear.
Examination of the ear by the aid of the auriscope.
Of or pertaining to the ear; as, aural medicine and surgery.
One skilled in treating and curing disorders of the ear.
Spontaneous generation.
Spontaneous or voluntary movement; movement due to an internal cause.
The process of artificially repairing lesions by taking a piece of healthy tissue, as from a neighboring part, to supply the deficiency caused by disease or wounds.
Capable of self-nourishment; -- said of all plants in which photosynthetic activity takes place, as opposed to parasitism or saprophytism.
Of or pertaining to the axilla or armpit; as, axillary gland, artery, nerve.
The science relating to bacteria.
Chemical decomposition brought about by bacteria without the addition of oxygen. The destruction or dissolution of bacterial cells.
The application of a knowledge of bacteria for their detection and identification, as in the examination of polluted water.
Of or pertaining to bacteria.
Destructive of bacteria.
Same as Germicide.
One skilled in bacteriology.
A microscopic vegetable organism. Certain species are active agents in fermentation, while others appear to be the cause of certain infectious diseases.
The middle of the anterior margin of the great foramen of the skull.
A muscle having two heads or origins; -- applied particularly to a flexor in the arm, and to another in the thigh.
Having two forms, bodies, or shapes.

The science of life; that branch of knowledge which treats of living matter as distinct from matter which is not living; the study of living tissue. It has to do with the origin, structure, development, function, and distribution of animals and plants.
A doctrine that the genesis or production of living organisms can take place only through the agency of living germs or parents. Life development generally.
The investigation of life.
1. The written history of a person's life. 2. Biographical writings in general.
The destruction of life.
Measurement of life; calculation of the probable duration of human life.

A name suggested by Dr. Beale for the germinal matter supposed to be essential to the functions of all living beings; the material through which every form of life manifests itself; unaltered protoplasm.
A tiny mass of bioplasm, in itself a living unit and having formative power, as a living white blood corpuscle; bioblast.
A view of life.
Relating to life; as, the biotic principle.
Relating or belonging to bile; conveying bile; as, biliary acids; biliary ducts. Biliary calculus, a gallstone, or a concretion formed in the gall bladder or its duct.

1. Of or pertaining to the bile. 2. Disordered in respect to the bile; troubled with and excess of bile; as, a bilious patient; dependent on, or characterized by, an excess of bile; as, bilious symptoms.
Multiplication or increase by gemmation or budding.
Inflammation of the eyelids.
Pertaining or belonging to the arm; as, the brachial artery; the brachial nerve.
The upper arm; the segment of the fore limb between the shoulder and the elbow.
An instrument for cutting into the bronchial tubes.
An incision into the windpipe or larynx, including the operations of tracheotomy and laryngotomy.
The bronchial tubes which arise from the branching of the trachea, esp. the subdivision of the bronchi. Dunglison.
Inflammation, acute or chronic, of the bronchial tubes or any part of them.
One of the subdivisions of the trachea or windpipe; esp. one of the two primary divisions.
Of or pertaining to the mouth or cheeks.
Of or pertaining to a bursa.
Inflammation of a bursa.
A condition of ill health and impairment of nutrition due to impoverishment of the blood, esp. when caused by a specific morbid process.
One of the bones of the tarsus which in man, forms the great bone of the heel; -- called also fibulare.
The operation of forming a new canthus, when one has been destroyed by injury or disease.
The corner where the upper and under eyelids meet on each side of the eye.
Headlike in form; also, having the distal end enlarged and rounded.
The incision of a capsule, esp. of that of the crystalline lens, as in a cataract operation.
Of or pertaining to a capsule; having the nature of a capsula; hollow and fibrous. Capsular ligament, a ligamentous bag or capsule surrounding many movable joints in the skeleton.
Inclosed in a capsule, or as in a chest or box.
Inflammation of a capsule, as that of the crystalline lens.
The depertment of zoology which treats of the Crustacea (lobsters, crabs, etc.); -- called also malacostracology and crustaceology.
A cancer. By some medical writers, the term is applied to an indolent tumor.
The curve or tracing made by a cardiograph.
An instrument which, when placed in contact with the chest, will register graphically the comparative duration and intensity of the heart's movements.
Description of the heart. Examination by the cardiograph.
Measurement of the heart, as by percussion or auscultation.
Induration of the heart, caused by development of fibrous tissue in the cardiac muscle.
Pertaining to, resembling, or hear the heart; as, the cardiac arteries; the cardiac, or left, end of the stomach.
Of or pertaining to the carpus, or wrist. One of the bones or cartilages of the carpus.
The wrist; the bones or cartilages between the forearm, or antibrachium, and the hand or forefoot; in man, consisting of eight short bones disposed in two rows.
Backwards; toward the tail or posterior part.Pertaining to, a tail; having a tail-like appendage.
Blindness.
Relating to the abdomen, or to the cavity of the abdomen.
An inflammantion of the cellular or areolar tissue, esp. of that lying immediately beneath the skin.
A peculiar rounded body lying near the nucleus of a cell. It is regarded as the dynamic element by means of which the machinery of cell division is organized.
Placed in the center or middle; central. At York or some other centrical place.
The body, or axis, of a vertebra.
The science which treats of the head.
An instrument measuring the dimensions of the head of a fetus during delivery.
The measurement of the heads of living persons.
An instrument for cutting into the fetal head, to facilitate delivery.
Dissection or opening of the head. Craniotomy; -- usually applied to bisection of the fetal head with a saw.
The act or operation of crushing the head of a fetus in the womb in order to effect delivery.
Having a head.
Forwards; towards the head or anterior extremity of the body; opposed to caudad.
Pain in the head; headache.
Having a head.
Of or pertaining to the head.
Shaped like the head.
Pertaining to the cerebellum.
The large lobe of the hind brain in front of and above the medulla; the little brain. It controls combined muscular action. See Brain.
The science which treats of the cerebrum or brain.
A hypochondriacal condition verging upon insanity, occurring in those whose brains have been unduly taxed; -- called also brain fag.
Examination of the brain for the diagnosis of diseas; esp., the act or process of diagnosticating the condition of the brain by examination of the interior of the eye (as with an ophthalmoscope).
Of or pertaining to the cerebrum. Cerebral apoplexy.
To exhibit mental activity; to have the brain in action.
Inflammation of the cerebrum.
Resembling, or analogous to, the cerebrum or brain.
A sugarlike body obtained by the decomposition of the nitrogenous non-phosphorized principles of the brain.
The anterior, and in man the larger, division of the brain; the seat of the reasoning faculties and the will. See Brain.
Pertaining to, or secreting, cerumen (earwax); as, the ceruminous glands.
Of or pertaining to the neck; as, the cervical vertebrae.
The process of forming an artificial tip or part of a lip, by using for the purpose a piece of healthy tissue taken from some neighboring part.
A term sometimes applied to the decomposition of organic substance into more simple bodies, by the use of chemical agents alone.
Inflammatory swelling of the conjunctival tissue surrounding the cornea.
A person versed in chemistry or given to chemical investigation; an analyst; a maker or seller of chemicals or drugs.
The tumid upper lip of certain mammals, as of a camel.
The art or practice of using the manual alphabet or of communicating thoughts by sings made by the hands and fingers.
One who communicates thoughts by signs made with the hands and fingers.
The green sickness; an anemic disease of young women, characterized by a greenish or grayish yellow hue of the skin, weakness, palpitation, etc.
Pertaining to, or obtained from, bile; as, choleic acid.
The development of cartilage.
The science which treats of cartilages.
The dissection of cartilages.
An inflammation of cartilage.
Resembling cartilage.
A cartilaginous tumor or growth.
Pertaining to the choroid coat.
An embryonic cell which develops into a pigment cell.
The state of being colored, as in the case of images formed by a lens.

Relating to time; according to time. Continuing for a long time; lingering; habitual. Chronic disease, one which is inveterate, of long continuance, or progresses slowly, in distinction from an acute disease, which speedly terminates.

The movement of the blood in the blood-vascular system, by which it is brought into close relations with almost every living elementary constituent. Also, the movement of the sap in the vessels and tissues of plants.
Promoting circulation; circulating.

Subserving the purposes of circulation; as, circulatory organs; of or pertaining to the organs of circulation; as, circulatory diseases. A chemical vessel consisting of two portions unequally exposed to the heat of the fire, and with connecting pipes or passages, through which the fluid rises from the overheated portion, and descends from the relatively colder, maintaining a circulation.

A disease of the liver in which it usually becomes smaller in size and more dense and fibrous in consistence; hence sometimes applied to similar changes in other organs, caused by increase in the fibrous framework and decrease in the proper substance of the organ.
Pertaining to, caused by, or affected with, cirrhosis; as, cirrhotic degeneration; a cirrhotic liver.
Capable of being coagulated.
That which produces coagulation.

Coagulated. To cause (a liquid) to change into a curdlike or semisolid state, not by evaporation but by some kind of chemical reaction; to curdle; as, rennet coagulates milk; heat coagulates the white of an egg. To undergo coagulation. To thicken; concrete; curdle; clot; congeal.
The thick, curdy precipitate formed by the coagulation of albuminous matter; any mass of coagulated matter, as a clot of bloot.
An operation for opening the colon.

A severe paroxysmal pain in the abdomen, due to spasm, obstruction, or distention of some one of the hollow viscera. Of or pertaining to colic; affecting the bowels. Of or pertaining to the colon; as, the colic arteries.
An inflammation of the large intestine, esp. of its mucous membrane; colonitis.
Latin word meaning neck or cervix. Same as Collar.
Relating to, or resembling, coma; drowsy; lethargic; as, comatose sleep; comatose fever.
Possessing the faculty of knowing one's own thoughts or mental operations. Some are thinking or conscious beings, or have a power of thought.
A plastic operation on the pupil, as for forming an artificial pupil.
Of a texture resembling horn; horny; hard.
Pertaining to the cornea.
One of the corneas of a compound eye in the invertebrates.
Of or pertaining to a corona. A suture extending across the skull between the parietal and frontal bones; the frontoparietal suture.
Of or pertaining to a crown. Resembling, or situated like, a crown or circlet; as, the coronary arteries and veins of the heart.
Having a crest or a crownlike appendage.
Relating to or denoting a hooked projection of bone.
Having a body; consisting of, or pertaining to, a material body or substance; material; -- opposed to spiritual or immaterial.
Relating to the outer layer of the cerebrum.
Having a special outer covering of a nature unlike the interior part.
An instrument (chisel or shears) to cut the ribs and open the thoracic cavity, in post-mortem examinations and dissections.
Pertaining to the ribs or the sides of the body; as, costal nerves. Relating to a costa, or rib.
Having ribs, or the appearance of ribs.
The department of science (as of ethnology or archeology) which deals with the shape, size, proportions, indications, etc., of skulls; the study of skulls.
An instrument for measuring the size of skulls.
The art or act of measuring skulls.
Scientific examination of the cranium.
The operation of opening the fetal head, in order to effect delivery.
Of or pertaining to the cranium.
One proficient in craniology; a phrenologist.
The skull of an animal; especially, that part of the skull, either cartilaginous or bony, which immediately incloses the brain; the brain case or brainpan. See Skull.
Of or pertaining to the thigh or leg, or to any of the parts called crura; as, the crural arteries; crural arch; crural canal; crural ring.
1. Of or pertaining to the cubit or ulna; as, the cubital nerve; the cubital artery; the cubital muscle.
Of pertaining to the skin; existing on, or affecting, the skin; as, a cutaneous disease; cutaneous absorption; cutaneous respiration.
A disease in which the body is colored blue in its surface, arising usually from a malformation of the heart, which causes an imperfect arterialization of the blood; blue jaundice.
A bluish or purple discoloration of the skin, lips, and nail beds that occurs when there's not enough oxygen in the blood.
Relating to cyanosis; affected with cyanosis; as, a cyanotic patient; having the hue caused by cyanosis; as, a cyanitic skin.
Hernia in which the urinary bladder protrudes; vesical hernia.
A calculus formed in the bladder. Bladder stone.
A nucleated cell having an envelope or cell wall, as a red blood corpuscle or an epithelial cell; a cell concerned in growth.
A knife or instrument used in cystotomy.
The act or practice of opening cysts; esp., the operation of cutting into the bladder, as for the extraction of a calculus.
1. Having the form of, or living in, a cyst; as, the cystic entozoa. Pertaining to, or contained in, a cyst; esp., pertaining to, or contained in, either the urinary bladder or the gall bladder.
A white crystalline substance, C3H7NSO2, containing sulphur, occuring as a constituent of certain rare urinary calculi, and occasionally found as a sediment in urine.
Inflammation of the bladder.
Resembling a cyst or bladder. A tissue mass, such as a tumour, that resembles a cyst but lacks an outer membrane.
The nucleus of a cell; the germinal or active spot of a cellule, through or in which cell development takes place.
Development of cells in animal and vegetable organisms.
Of or pertaining to cytogenesis or cell development.
Cell-like; -- applied to the corpuscles of lymph, blood, chyle, etc.
